summary: Pin cohort race with canary mirroring causes silent degraded fallback path
description: Issue summary: Customer (Lyra Health, Dedicated) reports increased proportion of requests routed to degraded fallback variant during a scheduled canary mirror update. Impact: ~6% of tenant traffic observed returning responses from the degraded variant without explicit pin loss; customer reports increased latency and reduced quality. Symptoms surfaced after a mirror prewarm operation coinciding with a canary weight shift.
impact: Customer-critical: affects production traffic for multiple endpoints. Observed increased 5xx fallback rates and 30-150ms higher p95 latency for affected tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a weighted canary rollout with traffic mirror prewarm enabled for model redwood-v2-small.
2) Start a dedicated capacity prewarm on pool DED-US-EAST-3 while pushing a small canary weight (5%).
3) Trigger tenant traffic with consistent session-affinity tokens and long-lived streaming sessions.
4) Observe cohort pin mapping and fallback routing in edge-proxy logs; note occasional silent diversion to degraded variant without explicit unpin event.
logs: edge-proxy[2026-03-12T15:21:42Z] tenant=lyra-001 route=api.chat model=redwood-v2-small routed_to=variant-degraded reason=fallback_path_no_unpin
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Mirroring/prewarm and cohort commit overlapped. We see a commit_delayed on cohort-reconciler when mirror attach completed; edge-proxy saw requests with cohort cookie but orchestrator had partial snapshot, causing routing decision to consult fallback path rather than honor pin.
Hypothesis 1: Prewarm mirror attach merges a shadow snapshot that does not include latest pin binding; if cohort commit is delayed, edge uses legacy mapping plus fallback policy (degraded variant).

Hypothesis 2: KV-cache mismatch (cohort-level KV) leads serving-runtime to mark session as stale and route to degraded fallback even though pin exists at control-plane—timing window where control-plane and edge disagree.
Observed: Approximately 4-7% of requests from Lyra tenants in the affected pool hit degraded variant for 2-5 minutes after mirror attach events. No explicit unpin was recorded in audit logs.
Metrics: spike in fallback_rate metric (fallback_rate.tenant.lyra-001) from 0.3% -> 6.2% at 2026-03-12T15:21Z; cohort_commit_latency spiked to 18s for the prewarm cycle.
Related signals: increased prewarm_attach_latency, orchestrator-snapshot-merge errors (transient), edge cache TTL expiration aligned with spike.
root_cause: Race condition between mirror prewarm snapshot merge and cohort pin commit. Edge proxy resolves routing before cohort commit completes; due to KV-cache state mismatch the request is routed to a fallback/degraded variant despite control-plane pin still pending commit.
workaround: 1) Force cohort reconcile for affected tenant (api: POST /internal/cohort/reconcile?tenant=lyra-001) to reapply pin snapshot. 2) Temporarily disable prewarm-mirror for scheduled canary windows for this customer's pool. 3) For affected requests, customer can set explicit model override in route header (x-redwood-model: redwood-v2-small) until fix is deployed.
fix_plan: Short term: Add guard in orchestrator to delay mirror snapshot activation until cohort commit ack received (rollback window 30s).
Medium term: Instrument additional consistency checks in edge-proxy to prefer committed pin mapping over fallback when commit_timestamp within 60s of mirror event.
Long term: Remove the shared shadow-snapshot path between mirror and commit; switch to atomic snapshot swap for pin metadata.
Owner: orchestrator team; PR being prepared to add commit ack gate.
